FARRA:v3p194/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p194/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p194/r8.claim: Multaḥad means a refuge or a passage in which one can seek shelter.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p323#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p323#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p323#3/r1.claim: Qatada glosses multahad as a refuge.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p492/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p492/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p492/r1.claim: Multaḥad means a place to turn aside to or seek refuge in.

TUSTARI:72:22/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:72:22/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:72:22/r1.claim: The command teaches dependence on and refuge in God, and to express that dependence; this guides believers and further misleads disbelievers. True monotheism attends to, turns toward, and relies on God alone, rejecting all else.

TAB-FULL:v23p348#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p348#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p348#2/r1.claim: No one among creation can protect or help the Prophet from God if God intends something for him.

TAB-FULL:v23p348#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p348#2/r2.speaker: حضرمي
TAB-FULL:v23p348#2/r2.claim: A report says a prominent jinn declared he would protect Muhammad, after which this verse was revealed.

TAB-FULL:v23p349/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p349/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p349/r1.claim: Multaḥad means a refuge or shelter to which one might flee from God.

TAB-FULL:v23p349/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p349/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p349/r2.claim: Qatāda glosses it as a refuge and helper.

TAB-FULL:v23p349/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p349/r3.speaker: سفيان
TAB-FULL:v23p349/r3.claim: Sufyān also interprets it as a refuge or supporter.

NAHHAS:v5p52/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p52/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p52/r6.claim: Lan marks the future; multahad is a refuge or place to lean toward, related to the side niche in a grave.

SULAMI:v2p354#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p354#2/r1.speaker: القاسم
SULAMI:v2p354#2/r1.claim: The declaration expresses sincerity and oneness: true tawhid directs attention only to God, turning away from all else and relying on Him alone.

THALABI:v10p55/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p55/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p55/r10.claim: Multahad means a refuge one can turn toward.

THALABI:v10p55/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p55/r11.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v10p55/r11.claim: Qatada glosses multahad as help or victory.

THALABI:v10p55/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p55/r12.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v10p55/r12.claim: Al-Kalbi glosses multahad as an entrance into the earth like a tunnel.

THALABI:v10p55/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p55/r13.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v10p55/r13.claim: Al-Suddi glosses multahad as a dug trench.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p120/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p120/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p120/r5.claim: Abu al-Jawza reports from Ibn Masud that on the night of the jinn the Messenger drew a line at al-Hajun and advanced to them; when their leader Wardan offered to drive them away, the Messenger said none could protect him from God.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p120/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p120/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p120/r6.claim: The phrase may mean nobody can protect the Messenger even alongside God's protection, or from what God has decreed for him.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p120/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p120/r7.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p120/r7.claim: ملتحد means a refuge or fortified shelter.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p120/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p120/r8.speaker: أبو سعيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p120/r8.claim: ملتحد can mean a guardian or protector.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p120/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p120/r9.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p120/r9.claim: ملتحد can mean a route or path; a poem uses the word for a way out from God's decree.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p325#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p325#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p325#3/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that if the Prophet disobeyed God, no one could protect him from God.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p325#3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p325#3/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p325#3/r2.claim: Muqatil says the Meccans told the Prophet to stop preaching, promising that they would protect him.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p325#3/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p325#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p325#3/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas explains ملتحد as someone to whom the Prophet could turn for refuge.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p325#3/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p325#3/r4.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p325#3/r4.claim: Qatada defines ملتحد as a refuge and a place of protection.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p325#3/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p325#3/r5.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p325#3/r5.claim: Al-Kalbi defines ملتحد as an entrance or tunnel into the earth.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p325#3/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p325#3/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p325#3/r6.claim: Abu Ishaq derives ملتحد from لحد and explains it as an entry into the earth.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p325#3/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p325#3/r7.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p325#3/r7.claim: Al-Farra says it means either refuge or tunnel.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p325#3/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p325#3/r8.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p325#3/r8.claim: Ibn Qutayba glosses it as a deviation or turning aside.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p325#3/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p325#3/r9.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p325#3/r9.claim: Al-Mubarrad compares it to منعرجا and says التحد means to incline.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:22-27/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:22-27/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:22-27/r1.claim: The Prophet finds no refuge apart from God.

JISHUMI:v10p7124/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7124/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7124/r10.claim: Ijāra means protecting someone from harm reaching him; no one can protect against God because His power is complete.

JISHUMI:v10p7124/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7124/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7124/r11.claim: Multaḥad is a refuge reached by turning aside toward safety; its root refers to a path that veers from the straight line and also names the side niche of a grave.

JISHUMI:v10p7124/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7124/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7124/r12.claim: God grants protection but cannot be protected against, since no one can prevent His will because His power is complete.

JISHUMI:v10p7124/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7124/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7124/r4.claim: The Prophet must detach himself and rely on God alone, as shown by saying he controls neither harm nor guidance.

JISHUMI:v10p7125/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7125/r10.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v10p7125/r10.claim: Another reading is that the Prophet has no control over harm or guidance, only the ability to convey revelation with God's help.

JISHUMI:v10p7125/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7125/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7125/r11.claim: Other views say no one will protect the Prophet if he fails to deliver, while delivery makes God his protector; he is a messenger who holds only what God has given him.

JISHUMI:v10p7125/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7125/r12.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7125/r12.claim: Abu Muslim allows the exception to mean what God has conveyed and given to the Prophet, with no refuge apart from what God commanded him.

JISHUMI:v10p7125/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7125/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7125/r6.claim: When idolaters offered to protect the Prophet if he abandoned his message, revelation instructed him to say no one can protect against God, who has power by His own essence and cannot be restrained.

JISHUMI:v10p7125/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7125/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7125/r7.claim: The Prophet is to explain that God alone owns benefit and harm and knows the unseen; the Messenger's duty is to convey the message.

JISHUMI:v10p7125/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7125/r8.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v10p7125/r8.claim: Multaḥad can mean a refuge or a helper; al-Kalbi explains it as an underground entrance and al-Suddi as a fortress.

JISHUMI:v10p7125/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7125/r9.speaker: الحسن وأبو علي
JISHUMI:v10p7125/r9.claim: Except for conveying God's message: this is the Prophet's refuge and means of salvation.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p243#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p243#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p243#2/r4.claim: No one can protect the Messenger from God if he disobeys Him; ملتحد is a refuge or place to lean toward.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p243#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p243#2/r5.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p243#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddi glosses ملتحد as a stronghold.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p243#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p243#2/r6.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p243#2/r6.claim: Al-Kalbi glosses ملتحد as an underground entrance or burrow.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384#2/r5.claim: من دونه means from someone other than Him; ملتحد is a refuge one turns toward, related to the sense of deviation in ilḥād and the side niche of a grave.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p384#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p384#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p384#3/r1.claim: If the Prophet disobeys God, no one can protect him; the unbelievers had offered to shelter him if he abandoned his message.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p384#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p384#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p384#3/r2.claim: The term multaḥad is explained at al-Kahf 18:27.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:22/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:22/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:22/r1.claim: No one can shield the Prophet from God’s punishment if he seeks refuge in them; his opponents had offered to protect him if he abandoned his message.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:22/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:22/r2.speaker: أبو الجوزاء عن ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:72:22/r2.claim: Ibn Masud recounts accompanying the Prophet to al-Hajun on the night of the jinn; their leader Wardan offered to repel them, and the Prophet answered that no one could protect him from God.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:22/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:22/r3.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:72:22/r3.claim: Al-Mawardi offers two readings: no one can protect him alongside God’s protection, or no one can protect him from what God decrees.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:22/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:22/r4.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:72:22/r4.claim: Qatada says multahad means a refuge; he also glosses it as helper or patron.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:22/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:22/r5.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:72:22/r5.claim: Al-Suddi interprets multahad as a fortress.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:22/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:22/r6.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:72:22/r6.claim: Al-Kalbi says it means an underground entrance or burrow in which one might hide.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:22/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:22/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:22/r7.claim: Other views gloss it as a guardian, patron, place to turn, or path; the meanings converge, and a line of poetry uses the word for refuge from divine decree.

BAYDAWI-FULL:72:22-24/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:22-24/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:22-24/r1.claim: No one can protect the Messenger from God if He intends harm, and he will find no refuge; ملتحد derives from entering a niche.

BAYDAWI-FULL:72:22-24/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:22-24/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:22-24/r2.claim: بلاغ may except from lack of power, since conveying guides and benefits, or from refuge; alternatively it means unless I deliver God’s message, with preceding words supplying the omitted consequence.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#7/r1.claim: No one can shield the Prophet from God's punishment if he disobeys; Salih said similarly, “Who would help me against God if I disobeyed Him?” There is no refuge besides God.

QASHANI:72:22-24/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:72:22-24/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:72:22-24/r1.claim: The Prophet cannot be protected from God or find refuge if God wills harm or misguidance; if he cannot control his own benefit, harm, or guidance, he cannot control theirs.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p302/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p302/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p302/r3.claim: The Prophet says no one can protect him from God and that he has no refuge apart from God; قتادة gives a similar gloss, while al-Suddi says protection, al-Kalbi says an underground refuge, and others say helper or path.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p302/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p302/r4.speaker: الماوردي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p302/r4.claim: One view supplies a prior offer from Wardan, leader of the jinn, to remove the crowd; the Prophet answers that no one can protect him from God.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p302/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p302/r5.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p302/r5.claim: He takes the next exception as disconnected: no one can protect me, but if I convey the message God will show mercy; the protection is figurative because conveying causes God's protection.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p302/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p302/r6.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p302/r6.claim: Another reading makes the exception connected, or a substitute from ملتحدا after negation: the only refuge is conveying and obeying so God protects him.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p302/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p302/r7.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p302/r7.claim: He says the exception is disconnected because the message comes from God, not from besides Him, so it cannot fall under the phrase 'no refuge apart from Him.'

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p302/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p302/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p302/r8.claim: A disconnected analysis treats إن لا as conditional, with an omitted verb meaning 'if I do not convey'; the next segment supplies a poem showing the same omission.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p302/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p302/r9.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p302/r9.claim: He construes the phrase as 'I possess only conveying to you'; Abu Hayyan says this is far-fetched because of the long separation between the clauses.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p303/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p303/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p303/r1.claim: A cited poem illustrates the omitted conditional verb; the omission is recoverable from the preceding imperative, and من marks the starting point.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p303/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p303/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p303/r2.claim: Following Qatada, he reads 'I possess only conveying from God' and treats the statement that none can protect the Prophet as an inserted clarification of his helplessness.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p303/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p303/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p303/r3.claim: رسالاته may coordinate with بلاغا, or with الله in 'from God and His messages.'

SAMIN-DURR:72:22/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:72:22/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:72:22/r1.claim: ‘Multahadan’ is the object of ‘ajidu’, which here means to find, reach, or resort to; it means a path or destination and, in the poem, an escape or refuge.

SAMIN-DURR:72:22/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:72:22/r2.speaker: الشاعر
SAMIN-DURR:72:22/r2.claim: The cited anonymous poet uses ‘multahad’ for a way of escape or recourse from God’s decree.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p245/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p245/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p245/r2.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, and al-Suddi explain “no refuge” as no place of shelter; Qatada also glosses it as no protector or retreat.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p245/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p245/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p245/r3.claim: The exception for delivering God’s messages may qualify the Prophet’s lack of control over harm and guidance, or his inability to find refuge; only fulfilling the message assigned to him is his duty, as in another verse.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p195/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p195/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p195/r8.claim: If God intends harm, no one can protect the Prophet from Him; there is no refuge, detour, place of retreat, or stratagem outside God's authority.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p195/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p195/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p195/r9.claim: Multahad derives from the idea of leaning or turning away from truth toward falsehood.

DURR-FULL:v8p308/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p308/r1.speaker: حضرمى
DURR-FULL:v8p308/r1.claim: Al-Hadrami reports that a prominent jinn offered to protect Muhammad, claiming he would shelter him, and the verse was revealed in response.

DURR-FULL:v8p308/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p308/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p308/r2.claim: Ibn Masud recounts that the jinn chief Wardan offered to keep the jinn away from the Prophet, who replied that none could protect him from God.

BURSEVI:v10p153#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p153#2/r1.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v10p153#2/r1.claim: Inwardly, the Prophet cannot guide through limited, attributed existence; guidance belongs to God absolutely.

BURSEVI:v10p153#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p153#2/r2.speaker: القاشاني
BURSEVI:v10p153#2/r2.claim: Al-Qāshānī says guidance and misguidance belong to God; the Prophet cannot compel guidance.

BURSEVI:v10p153#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p153#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p153#2/r3.claim: Yujīrunī means rescue or protect; no one can save the Prophet from God’s force, punishment, or a harm God decrees.

BURSEVI:v10p153#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p153#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v10p153#2/r4.claim: Some say the expression signals pure monotheism: directing attention only to God requires turning to Him, away from all else, and relying on Him alone.

BURSEVI:v10p153#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p153#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p153#2/r5.claim: Multaḥad means refuge or place of inclination; in distress no refuge or recourse exists except God, showing the Prophet cannot control even his own affairs.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p93#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p93#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p93#4/r1.claim: No one can protect the Prophet from God or provide a refuge apart from Him; ملتحد means a place or direction of refuge.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p93#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p93#4/r2.speaker: الكلبي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p93#4/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi glosses ملتحد as an entrance into the earth, while al-Suddi calls it a fortress; its root evokes an entrance or niche.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p93#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p93#4/r3.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v29p93#4/r3.claim: Al-Raghib allows ملتحد to be either a place noun or a verbal noun.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p93#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p93#4/r4.speaker: الماوردي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p93#4/r4.claim: Al-Mawardi reports a proposed context in which opponents tell the Prophet to abandon his message and promise protection; the author dismisses this and a similar jinn story.

ELMALILI:72:20-28/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:20-28/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:72:20-28/r4.claim: If the Prophet disobeyed God by worshiping another, no human, jinn, angel, or other being could rescue him from God's punishment.

ELMALILI:72:20-28/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:20-28/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:72:20-28/r5.claim: There is no refuge apart from God from His majesty or others' hostility; everyone is under His power, so worship and supplication belong to Him alone, as do people's fear and hope.

ELMALILI:72:20-28/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:20-28/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:72:20-28/r6.claim: One must not conclude before the exception that asking the Prophet for benefit is forbidden; the commentary rejects the Wahhabi claim that seeking his intercession or mediation in prayer is shirk.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p243/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p243/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p243/r6.claim: The two sentences about having no protector and no refuge interrupt the surrounding exception; they answer the demand that the Prophet stop condemning their beliefs and idols.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p243/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p243/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p243/r7.claim: ملتحد is a place of turning aside for refuge, especially an asylum; the meaning is that the Prophet will find no place to protect him.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p243/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p243/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p243/r8.claim: من دونه describes a refuge outside God's dominion, which cannot exist; لن therefore emphatically denies finding one.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p244/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p244/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p244/r1.claim: The من before دون is an extra preposition governing the adverb.

TABATABAI:72:20-23/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:20-23/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:72:20-23/r10.claim: The exception means the Prophet has no refuge other than delivering God's message; the phrase from God modifies an implied expression, since delivery takes ʿan, though some read min as ʿan.

TABATABAI:72:20-23/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:20-23/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:72:20-23/r6.claim: The Prophet is human, unable to cause people harm or guide them by his own power, and must obey God's command to preach without any refuge from God if he disobeys.

TABATABAI:72:20-23/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:20-23/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:72:20-23/r9.claim: Ijāra is granting protection, and multahad is a place one turns aside to escape harm; another gloss is an entrance.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p519/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p519/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p519/r6.claim: The Prophet must say that associating anyone with God to appease or fear his opponents would falsely attribute the gravest crime to God, for which no one can shelter him from divine punishment.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p520/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p520/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p520/r1.claim: The crime of associating partners with God brings punishment from which no one can provide refuge or asylum.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:20/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:20/r1.speaker: Mekkeli müşrikler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:20/r1.claim: The Meccan polytheists said they would protect Muhammad from his enemies if he abandoned the monotheistic message.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:20/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:20/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:20/r2.claim: The response makes clear that the Prophet cannot worship anyone but God and has no purpose beyond conveying the divine commands and message entrusted to him.

STUDYQURAN:72:21/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:72:21/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:72:21/r1.claim: The Prophet has no power beyond faithfully delivering God’s message, a recurring Quranic theme.

STUDYQURAN:72:21/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:72:21/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:72:21/r2.claim: Because Arabs tended toward idol worship, the Quran repeatedly rejects taking prophets or angels as lords, as in 3:79–80.
